name: Sun–Earth L2
story: The second Lagrange point — 1.5 million km from Earth, on the line from the Sun through Earth and out the back. The gravity of the Sun + Earth combine to keep a spacecraft station-keeping with minimal fuel. Always-night sky, always-warm Earth-facing side, the same Sun angle forever — the perfect parking spot for infrared telescopes that need to stay cold and pointed away from the Sun. JWST is parked here, in a halo orbit ~800,000 km wide.
comparison: Four times farther than the Moon. The Sun, Earth, and Moon all sit on one side of the spacecraft, simplifying the sunshield geometry.

firsts.label: Herschel + Planck — first ESA L2 missions
